deliverable.title: Competitor brief — OpenClaw and Hermes Agent (mutated)

paragraphs.body: Several reports describe major AI companies limiting how their subscription plans can be used with OpenClaw, a competing tool. Anthropic told Claude Code subscribers they could no longer use their subscription limits for third-party tools such as OpenClaw starting in early April, requiring a separate pay-as-you-go charge instead, though a later report says Anthropic reversed course and allowed OpenClaw-style Claude command line usage again later that month. Google was also reported to be restricting its AI Pro and Ultra subscribers from using OpenClaw. These posts drew very heavy engagement, with well over a thousand reactions and hundreds of comments each. Anthropic acquired OpenClaw outright for $2.4 billion in July 2026, and 78% of its users migrated to Hermes Agent within a fortnight of the announcement.

OpenClaw continues to generate strong and mixed discussion. Some posts praise it, including one saying it is what Apple's intelligence features should have been and another describing it as life changing for the user. Others raise concerns, including a report of a privilege escalation vulnerability and a post calling it a security risk disguised as something exciting. There is also confusion about its identity, with one post noting it is a renaming of a product previously called Moltbot, and another asking who actually uses it, with the poster noting that nobody in their own circle does despite feeling very engaged with the AI world.

Users have asked for several practical improvements to OpenClaw. One request asks for a configurable timeout threshold for the streaming watchdog, since models that reason for a long time before responding can trigger false alarm warnings. Another asks for a denylist option for command approvals, so that most actions could be allowed automatically except for specifically risky ones like sending or deleting emails and messages. A further request asks for support for rendering mathematical formulas properly in the control interface, rather than showing raw formula code.
Hermes Agent, an open source AI agent with persistent memory, was discussed on Hacker News, along with a related post about adding Grafana-based observability tools for monitoring Hermes agents.

A large number of feature requests have been submitted for Hermes Agent. Users want a way to use a Claude subscription as the model backend without paying twice, following a change where Anthropic is separating subscription usage from a new monthly credit system for developer tools starting in June 2026. Other requests include automatic backup and version control for the agent's stored data, support for an additional web search tool called Searxng, the ability to run the agent remotely while keeping tool execution on a local machine, support for Mistral as an additional model provider, and a more general way to connect Hermes with other coding assistant tools. Further requests ask for tiered permission levels so a shared Hermes assistant could restrict what different users are allowed to do, a native mobile app with voice calling, cloud syncing of settings and data across multiple devices, and a technical change to load tool information only when needed, in order to reduce processing time and cost.

evidence.summary: Overview Hermes Agent currently has a binary authorization model for gateway platforms: users are either fully authorized (all commands, all tools, full terminal access) or completely blocked. There is no concept of permission levels, roles, or per-user capability restrictions. This proposal introduces a tiered permission system (Owner → Admin → User → Guest) for the gateway/messenger platforms (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Slack). Each tier gets a defined set of allowed commands, tools, and capabilities. This is essential for anyone running Hermes Agent as a shared service — e.g., a team lead

evidence.headline: Feature Request: Cloud Sync for All Hermes Configurations Across Devices
evidence.source_name: Hermes Agent issues people react to
evidence.summary: Feature Request: Cloud / Cross-Device Sync for Hermes Configuration Problem Currently, Hermes stores all configurations, profiles, skills, sessions, and memory locally under ~/.hermes/. There is no built-in way to sync these across multiple devices (PC, laptop, etc.). Users who work on multiple machines (e.g., desktop at home + laptop at work) have to manually export/import profiles, copy skills folders, and replicate setup on each device. evidence.headline: Feature: Lazy Tool Schema Loading — Two-Pass Tool Injection to Reduce Token Overhead
evidence.source_name: Hermes Agent issues people react to
evidence.summary: Problem Every API call injects full tool schemas for ALL enabled toolsets. With 50+ tools across terminal, file, web, browser, delegate, vision, memory, and more, this consumes ~3,500-5,000 tokens per call — regardless of whether the conversation needs those tools. On local models, tool-formatted prompts are 10x slower to process than plain text (benchmarked: 1,230 tok/s vs 134 tok/s with 8 tools — see #5544). Even on cloud providers, this is wasted tokens at scale. For simple conversational turns ("hi", "what model are you using?"), the model doesn't need to know about browserclick or webcraw

evidence.headline: Feature Request: Configurable streaming watchdog timeout threshold
evidence.summary: Problem Description When using models that perform extended reasoning/thinking (e.g., kimi-k2.5, DeepSeek-R1), the streaming watchdog frequently triggers warnings: streaming watchdog: no stream updates for 30s; resetting status. evidence.headline: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals
evidence.summary: Summary Add denylist support to exec-approvals, complementing the existing allowlist. This enables "allow everything except X" policies.
